To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
in Brittany and Scotland the development of bilingual primary education has been shaped by a complex interaction of policy and politics.

, despite their different historical and cultural trajectories, Brittany and Scotland are both territories in which minority language education has been developed, albeit in different ways, in the context of the institutionalisation of bilingualism in public-sector education.
the Breton case shows that the political will to develop minority-language education can be generated by the political class and that the Gaelic case demonstrates that it can come from civil society.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ways in which minority language policies are implemented and institutionalised in public education.
the following questions: How do policy and politics interact?
the ways in which the politics of language and culture have been articulated through education, and with the ways in language and culture have become embedded within the education process itself.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the institutionalisation of minority language education in the public sector is a process that is not only driven by the state, but also by local communities.
Breton education has developed in a more ‘top-down’ manner, while the Scottish case has been much more ‘bottom-up’.

, while the institutionalisation of Breton and Gaelc in public-sector primary schools has been a slow and uneven process, the development of minority languages has been facilitated by the existence of strong political movements and by the creation of a favourable climate for the development of language policies.
The main takeaway from our work is that

it is important to recognise the role of the state in the development of minority language education, but also to acknowledge the role played by other actors, such as local government and non-governmental organisations, in shaping the policy process and the outcomes of that process.

it is not possible to understand the dynamics of minority language education without taking into account the politics of language, the politics of education, and the politics of the region or nation in which they are embedded.
policy and politics are not simply separate spheres of activity, but are intimately linked in complex and dynamic ways.
